problem: It takes $4$ hours for a marathon runner to run $20$ miles at a constant pace. How long does it take for the marathon runner to run $26$ miles?

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating Time Given Distance and Speed
examples.problem: It takes $5$ days for the Earth to travel $13$ million kilometers around the Sun. How much time does it take for the Earth to travel $52$ million kilometers around the Sun?
examples.worked_solution:
Speed is a special unit rate applied to moving objects. It is defined as *the distance traveled per unit of time*:

$$
\text{speed} = \dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}
$$

To find the speed, in millions of kilometers per day, we divide the number of million kilometers, $13,$ by the number of days, $5.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{13}{5} & =13÷5 \\  & =2.6.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the speed of the Earth is $2.6$ million kilometers per day. 

To find the time it takes the Earth to cover $52$ million kilometers, we divide the distance by $2.6.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{time} & =\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}} \\  & =\frac{52}{2.6} \\  & =\frac{52\times 10}{2.6\times 10} \\  & =\frac{520}{26} \\  & =520÷26 \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, it takes the Earth $20$ days to travel $52$ million kilometers around the Sun.

feedback.problem: A spacecraft traveled for $15$ seconds at a constant speed of $12$ kilometers per second. Find the distance covered by the spacecraft.
feedback.worked_solution:
The speed is $12$ kilometers per second. To find the distance covered in $15$ seconds, we multiply the speed by $15.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{distance} & =\text{speed}\cdot \text{time} \\  & =12\times 15 \\  & =180.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the spacecraft covered $180$ kilometers in $15$ seconds.
